bets.verdict: Results are in, and you know the house rule by now: I read them out whether they flatter me or not. And it’s a green one — the slip did exactly what the numbers said it would, which is the most satisfying sentence in this whole trade. I told you the Maardu Linnameeskond v Tallinna FC Flora U21 defences were held together with tape, and 5 goals later the scoreboard read 3-2 — that’s the form table talking, not luck. On we go — the season is a marathon of small edges, and yesterday, whatever it was, is now just one more data point behind us.

Let me walk you through how yesterday actually went, because a record only means something if somebody’s honest about it every single morning. Both slips down, hands up from me. I deal in edges, and edges mean sometimes the percentages take a day off — the long game is where we win, and the long game continues tomorrow. The leg that cost us was Brommapojkarna v GAIS at 1-1 — I read an open game and got a chess match, and I’ll hold my hands up: the goals simply never came. Whatever yesterday gave us, today asks a new question — and I’ll have an answer on the board by breakfast, same as always.

The slips are settled and the kettle’s on, so here’s your report from the Gaffer — no spin, no hiding, just what happened. Half glory, half grumbling: the double did everything asked of it, the treble had one leg too ambitious. That’s trebles for you — bigger pay-off, more ways to break your heart. The star of the show was Odd against Haugesund — 4 goals in it, finished 1-3, and honestly the over was home before some of you had found your seats. Where did it go wrong? FC Seoul against Incheon United, that’s where — a 1-0 borefest from two teams who’d scored for fun all month and picked yesterday to remember how to defend. Right, that’s the accounting done — now if you’ll excuse me, tomorrow’s form tables aren’t going to squint at themselves.

Morning, you lot. Before we talk about today’s card, we settle up yesterday’s like grown-ups. It was a day of two halves, this — the double marched home without breaking sweat, but the treble found the one result on the card with other ideas. Egersund v Moss did everything I said it would and then some — 3-0 at the whistle, and the over sailed home with time to spare. The dud was the both-teams-to-score in Degerfors v Malmö FF — Degerfors couldn’t buy a goal at 0-1, and one shy front line is all it takes to sink that market. Long game, this — one day never makes us and one day never breaks us, which is exactly why the record stays public and the method stays the same.

The pick of the winners was the Ranheim game — 2-5, 7 goals for the greedy, and the sweet feeling of watching a form read play out to the letter. One team turned up in Drogheda United v Bohemians and it wasn’t Drogheda United — 0-2, no both-teams-scored, and there’s your loser, named and shamed. That’s yesterday filed — today’s card is already on my desk, the coffee’s fresh, and the value doesn’t find itself. Back shortly with the picks.

I’ve had my coffee and read the scores twice, so here it is — yesterday’s verdict, straight from the man who picked them. Not our day, simple as that — the card went against us leg by leg, and I’d rather show you the loss in full than pretend it didn’t happen. Honest record, honest morning. The leg that let us down was the corners in Thór v KR — the game stayed narrow, the flags stayed still, and the count fell short of the line. We log it, we learn from it, and we go again — the beautiful thing about this game is there’s always another card tomorrow, and I intend to read it better than the bookies do.
